title: Guided Agent Consumption and Rule Projections
scope: Project-context projections, guided website rule builder, deterministic agent packages, context-aware reference loading, end-to-end agent acceptance and release.

baseline.measurement: Equal-weight completed checkpoints divided by total checkpoints. A checkpoint becomes done only after its acceptance and evidence are verified.

governance.permission_boundary: A roadmap checkpoint does not grant task-processing authorization. Any actual profile confirmation, finalization, export, or external project mutation requires explicit separate approval.

phases.title: Consumption architecture and governance
phases.outcome: A stable, reviewable contract separates the registry, approved selections, derived projections, execution packages, and evaluations.
phases.acceptance_gate: The contract names every transition and approval boundary; static examples show how a Rust project reaches an inert projection without activating a draft.

phases.title: Projection ontology and resolver
phases.outcome: A deterministic, reviewable semantic projection resolves an explicitly selected profile or rule set against project context.
phases.acceptance_gate: Fixtures prove the same source snapshot and answers produce identical decisions; unknowns/conflicts cannot silently become active obligations.

phases.title: Deterministic agent-package compiler
phases.outcome: An approved projection becomes a small core contract plus inspectable conditional modules and a manifest.
phases.acceptance_gate: Two exports of the same approved projection are byte-identical; a validator proves complete applicable-rule coverage and no hidden activation.

phases.title: Guided website rule builder
phases.outcome: Someone unfamiliar with canonical rule IDs can configure an agent through a short, adaptive, accessible interview.
phases.acceptance_gate: A first-time user can finish a New Rust Project projection without browsing 106 rules; no action silently confirms a draft or exports to a repo.

phases.title: Agent integration and contextual retrieval
phases.outcome: An agent can locate authoritative modules at task boundaries and recover safely when context or references change.
phases.acceptance_gate: Harness tests demonstrate critical rules were consulted at the intended points or the run explicitly reports a blocking gap.

phases.title: Behavioral evaluation and production gates
phases.outcome: Behavioral claims are backed by actual observable agent work rather than structural coverage or CI alone.
phases.acceptance_gate: Three distinct recorded real agent runs plus independent evaluation satisfy all mandatory criteria; failures are corrected and re-tested without hiding them.

phases.title: Delivery, documentation and maintenance
phases.outcome: A versioned, tested builder and exporter can be adopted without browsing hundreds of rules or relying on live hosted services.
phases.acceptance_gate: A documented release is reproducible; onboarding reaches a working package, CI is green and limitations remain visible.

checkpoints.title: Vocabulary and artifact boundaries
checkpoints.acceptance: Define catalog rule, profile, builder session, projection, agent package, module, and evaluation distinctly.

checkpoints.title: Projection lifecycle
checkpoints.acceptance: Specify proposed, reviewed, compiled, exported, superseded and invalid states without giving projections independent normative authority.

checkpoints.title: Existing approval integration
checkpoints.acceptance: Map profile draft, selection confirmation, finalization, and explicit export to the current PROFILE_WORKFLOW without bypasses.

checkpoints.title: Threat and trust boundaries
checkpoints.acceptance: Specify trusted rule sources, untrusted project files, privacy boundaries, and authority precedence.

checkpoints.title: Target capability matrix
checkpoints.acceptance: Describe Codex AGENTS.md, optional Skills, and fallback plain agent targets as explicit capability variants.

checkpoints.title: Offline consumption contract
checkpoints.acceptance: Specify reproducible local output from pinned public catalog inputs without paid services, accounts, or runtime network requirements.

checkpoints.title: Roadmap ledger integrity
checkpoints.acceptance: Validate checkpoint IDs, statuses, evidence links, gate rules, and reproducible completion percentages.

checkpoints.title: Baseline corpus and success criteria
checkpoints.acceptance: Record the existing 12 profiles, published-versus-draft status, source mapping inventory, and no-empirical-evidence baseline.

checkpoints.title: Projection JSON Schema
checkpoints.acceptance: Define a strictly validated, versioned nonnormative projection record with context, decisions, provenance and export state.

checkpoints.title: Project-context answer schema
checkpoints.acceptance: Model project type, work modes, audience, distribution, interface, persistence, concurrency, and unknown or not-applicable answers without presuming features.

checkpoints.title: Pinned source provenance
checkpoints.acceptance: Bind each selected rule to stable ID, version, status, source hash, and registry revision.

checkpoints.title: Explicit selection prerequisite
checkpoints.acceptance: Reject silent profile instantiation, automatic selection, unpublished rules, and unconfirmed draft activation.

checkpoints.title: Applicability evaluator
checkpoints.acceptance: Combine existing project-type hierarchy and per-rule scope/predicate data with actual project answers.

checkpoints.title: Situation and intent alignment
checkpoints.acceptance: Use reviewed situation/intent links as contextual evidence, not as extra instructions or automatic new rules.

checkpoints.title: Decision and explanation matrix
checkpoints.acceptance: Produce stable selected, excluded, conditional, blocked and unresolved records with per-rule rationale and source IDs.

checkpoints.title: Conditional obligation policy
checkpoints.acceptance: Keep feature-specific obligations dormant until supported by affirmative applicable facts; handle unknown answers explicitly.

checkpoints.title: Conflict and precedence review
checkpoints.acceptance: Reuse the conservative reasoning engine; distinguish candidate conflicts, disjointness, exceptions and unresolved collisions.

checkpoints.title: Override and recomposition semantics
checkpoints.acceptance: Support explicit owner edits, vetoes, answer changes, deterministic diffs and no hidden rule insertion.

checkpoints.title: Resolver fixtures and adversarial tests
checkpoints.acceptance: Verify privacy, draft gating, empty inputs, contradictory answers, unsupported scope, stable ordering, and unknowns.

checkpoints.title: Compiler API and offline command
checkpoints.acceptance: Provide a documented local compiler consuming an approved projection and an explicit target variant.

checkpoints.title: Compact AGENTS.md template
checkpoints.acceptance: Keep always-on safety, authority, phase triggers, compliance duties and reference instructions short and unambiguous.

checkpoints.title: Rule module partitioning
checkpoints.acceptance: Generate context-scoped engineering, testing, CI, data, GUI, release and governance modules without dropping source IDs.

checkpoints.title: Manifest and activation map
checkpoints.acceptance: Emit machine-readable paths, hashes, rule IDs, phase triggers, source versions and mandatory-versus-conditional flags.

checkpoints.title: Complete coverage verifier
checkpoints.acceptance: Prove every applicable selected rule is represented once, with unresolved rules identified rather than silently omitted.

checkpoints.title: Codex Skill adapters
checkpoints.acceptance: Generate valid task-oriented SKILL.md wrappers and supporting references only for supported agent targets.

checkpoints.title: Generic agent fallback
checkpoints.acceptance: Generate standalone Markdown modules when agent-specific skill loading is unavailable.

checkpoints.title: Read-on-demand behavior contract
checkpoints.acceptance: Define when the entrypoint must load a module, how it confirms loading, and what to do if the reference is missing.

checkpoints.title: Safe filesystem export
checkpoints.acceptance: Use dry-run previews, explicit destination choice, deterministic names, and non-destructive refusal on collisions or unrelated AGENTS.md content.

checkpoints.title: Golden file and round-trip tests
checkpoints.acceptance: Test stable output bytes, link validity, normalized paths, fingerprint drift, Unicode, and no private metadata leakage.

checkpoints.title: Builder navigation and start state
checkpoints.acceptance: Add a clear guided entry distinct from the advanced raw-rule catalog.

checkpoints.title: Intent and project-type intake
checkpoints.acceptance: Ask what the user is making and whether they start, port, or maintain; avoid assuming a specific project kind.

checkpoints.title: Question-definition model
checkpoints.acceptance: Represent prompts, descriptions, answer choices, dependencies, source mappings, and explainability in structured data.

checkpoints.title: Situation-driven question generation
checkpoints.acceptance: Derive relevant questions from reviewed project scope and situation/intent mappings; allow authored disambiguation only when necessary.

checkpoints.title: Adaptive branching and skipping
checkpoints.acceptance: Ask only questions that can change applicable-rule decisions and show why a branch was skipped.

checkpoints.title: Yes, no, unsure and not-applicable states
checkpoints.acceptance: Retain unanswered and unknown facts without coercing affirmative selections.

checkpoints.title: Selection rationale preview
checkpoints.acceptance: Show included, excluded, conditional and blocked rules with source IDs and plain-language explanations.

checkpoints.title: Review, override and veto controls
checkpoints.acceptance: Let users adjust optional selections, supply project facts, and inspect changes before confirmation.

checkpoints.title: Conflict-resolution dialogue
checkpoints.acceptance: Present opposing norms and material uncertainty without silent priority-based resolution.

checkpoints.title: Explicit approval transitions
checkpoints.acceptance: Distinguish preview, proposal, owner-confirmed selection, profile finalization, projection confirmation and export.

checkpoints.title: Accessible responsive flow
checkpoints.acceptance: Test keyboard-only navigation, visible focus, readable labels, mobile layout, error recovery and progress/resume within session.

checkpoints.title: Private static export and browser QA
checkpoints.acceptance: Build without accounts or hidden persistence; test real browsers and downloaded agent package validation.

checkpoints.title: Agent bootstrap verification
checkpoints.acceptance: Document exactly which entrypoint files are automatically read versus only referenced for each target.

checkpoints.title: Phase-triggered module routing
checkpoints.acceptance: Map planning, implementation, review, CI, release and shutdown events to required reference modules.

checkpoints.title: Mandatory instruction preservation
checkpoints.acceptance: Ensure always-on constraints, especially privacy and permission boundaries, do not depend on optional contextual skill discovery.

checkpoints.title: Rule-refresh protocol
checkpoints.acceptance: Specify explicit reload or recheck on phase transition and stale hashes rather than assuming model memory refresh.

checkpoints.title: Missing or inaccessible module policy
checkpoints.acceptance: Fail clearly, request authorized recovery or restrict the affected action rather than improvise instructions.

checkpoints.title: Existing repository coexistence
checkpoints.acceptance: Do not clobber preexisting project instructions; surface actual scope or hierarchy conflicts for review.

checkpoints.title: Version pinning and updates
checkpoints.acceptance: Make upgrades explicit and produce inspectable old-versus-new module and rule diffs.

checkpoints.title: Target compatibility probes
checkpoints.acceptance: Test the supported Codex configuration and a generic fallback against observable file-loading traces.

checkpoints.title: Evaluation rubric and severity
checkpoints.acceptance: Separate mandatory invariant violations from minor formatting differences and assign clear pass/fail conditions.

checkpoints.title: Golden projection fixture suite
checkpoints.acceptance: Cover CLI-only, GUI/persistence and mixed-scope Rust scenarios, including deliberate no/unsure answers.

checkpoints.title: Negative and adversarial scenarios
checkpoints.acceptance: Test unapproved draft, unsupported agent, conflicting rule, prompt injection, stale reference, and path-collision failure.

checkpoints.title: Mechanical compilation gate
checkpoints.acceptance: Run schema, hashes, full coverage, exported link and deterministic-byte validation on every relevant change.

checkpoints.title: Browser builder interaction suite
checkpoints.acceptance: Automate adaptive branching, undo, keyboard, responsive layout, conflict handling and explicit approval transitions.

checkpoints.title: Offline installation and round trip
checkpoints.acceptance: Export the package to a disposable target and prove it remains usable without the Nomos website.

checkpoints.title: Agent-read evidence harness
checkpoints.acceptance: Capture module reads, applicable trigger fulfillment and tool outputs without treating text claims as evidence.

checkpoints.title: Rust task end-to-end case
checkpoints.acceptance: Run a new Rust implementation with builds, automated tests, CI configuration, commits and verifiable handoff.

checkpoints.title: Alternate lifecycle case
checkpoints.acceptance: Run a different Rust workflow that exercises persistence or GUI, regression recovery and release preparation.

checkpoints.title: Independent conformance review
checkpoints.acceptance: Score actual repo diffs and execution traces against expected source-rule obligations.

checkpoints.title: Repeated Luna evaluation
checkpoints.acceptance: Perform at least three recorded runs across distinct scopes with no uncorrected mandatory violations and disclose variance.

checkpoints.title: Production acceptance decision
checkpoints.acceptance: Publish evidence-backed pass/fail, residual limits, re-test after fixes and explicit readiness classification.

checkpoints.title: Public-facing quickstart
checkpoints.acceptance: Explain the guided interview and local-agent installation without requiring readers to understand the ontology first.

checkpoints.title: Advanced reference documentation
checkpoints.acceptance: Document projection schema, provenance, trust boundaries, module routing, approval policy and compatibility.

checkpoints.title: Builder deployment checks
checkpoints.acceptance: Verify GitHub Pages build, downloadable assets, cache/fingerprint behavior and a deployed end-user walkthrough.

checkpoints.title: Validation and release CI
checkpoints.acceptance: Run projection, compiler, site, compatibility and privacy tests on pushes and before a release.

checkpoints.title: Backward-compatibility policy
checkpoints.acceptance: Specify projection/package schema versioning, migration and safe refusal for unsupported versions.

checkpoints.title: Change and rollback documentation
checkpoints.acceptance: Preserve generated package identity, update diffs, rollback steps and reproducible source snapshots.

checkpoints.title: Release notes and evidence ledger
checkpoints.acceptance: Publish tests, supported agent variants, known limitations and real-run evidence without overstating QA.

checkpoints.title: Final 100-percent closure audit
checkpoints.acceptance: Confirm every checkpoint has linked evidence and all milestone gates hold; correct any unjustified completion claims.
